```
Command.registerCommand("luatest1",0,false,false,0,0,false,false,testFun)
```

*Iterators, Proxies, Pointers, and Memory*

The next real challenge was iterators.  The issue was memory.  Lua has essentially one basic data structure (other than primitive types): Tables.  Tables underlie everything eventually.  It's all just a lot of abstractions that are actually implemented in lua to extend the language.  

When first pondering the task of "return a list of the Characters in a room" I ran into an issue.  The list of players in a room is implemented in the mud as a linked list.  Unrolling and reading every element of that list to build a table could require quite a bit of memory (particularly considering that some of the lists in the game have tens of thousands structs hanging off of them).  Therefore, that option (building tables to return data) was right out for all but the most basic of tasks (more on that later).  The only other option was to implement iterator functions.  Fortunately, iterators turned out to have been extremely simple due to a design decision I made early on about the use of pointers as magic cookies.  

The issue is, if you have a handle to an object in the mud - in lua - what is that handle really?  Do you construct extra C representations of everything that the user could interact with in memory ahead of time?  That idea did not suit me at all.  Eventually I settled on using the pointers to the objects themselves as the references in lua.  To assure that proxy objects are dealt with properly on the C side of the layer, I adopted a convention in which handles are always dereferenced as their proxy objects.  This allows us to construct proxy objects on demand while also assuring that the lua layer can't have a handle to anything that does not have at least some substance within the game world (no ethereal objects).

```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- chars in room iterator and ch equivalence test function test
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
luaTestRoomChIter = function(ch,arg)
  ch:sendTo("&BYou are in a room called: " .. ch:getInRoom():getName().." along with:\n")
  for chIter in ch:getInRoom():characters() do
    -- if the ch is not equal to the chIter (don't print ourselves)
  	if(ch ~= chIter) then
  		ch:sendTo(chIter:getName().."\n")
  	end
  end
end
Command.registerCommand("luatest2",0,false,false,0,0,false,false,luaTestRoomChIter)
```

Eventually this test was "reused" to validate the implementation of object equivalence.  Due to the pointer cookie decision, this turned out to be quite easy.  If the pointers match, both handles refer to the same underlying mud object.  The development process did lead to the discovery of a potential memory leak regarding proxy objects however.

*The Journey into Objects*

Things in the room naturally folds directly into things in your inventory.  This is the beginning of the journey through implementing objects.

```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- object iterator test function -- wearing, carrying, in room
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- also demonstrates the isInstanceOf function which can test objects for 
-- their types.  Certain object types have special functions/attributes, like
-- containers and explosives.
--
-- It is a conscious design decision to not expose the raw properties of the 
-- objects in lua (the "value" fields).  These are obtuse enough as it is on 
-- the C side.  I don't want people making changes to them that are difficult
-- if not impossible to properly validate.  This adds some work, because
-- API functions need to be added to adjust every meaningful property
-- for every variety of object.  However, in the long run, it will help 
-- things in the Lua layer stay much more sane than they have tended to in
-- the core.
--
-- Also -- Objects in lua are never stacked.  They are unstacked as you iterate 
-- through them.  It is impossible to mishandle a stacked object here.
-- They are only unstacked as they are accessed from the iterator, so this 
-- does save a bit of memory.
luatest14 = function(ch,arg) 
  ch:sendTo("Wearing:\n\r")
  for objIter in ch:wearing() do
    -- test of obj:isValid() method
    if(objIter:isValid()) then
    	ch:sendTo(objIter:getName().."\n\r")
  		if(objIter:getType() == Object.Type.CONTAINER) then
                                                    --- Lua ternary operator http://lua-users.org/wiki/TernaryOperator
  			ch:sendTo("\t\tis a container and it is ".. (objIter:isEmpty() and "empty" or "not empty") .. "\n\r")
  		end      
      local flags = objIter:getExtraFlags()
      ch:sendTo("Flags\n\r")
      for k,v in pairs(flags) do
        ch:sendTo(k:tostring().." ")
      end
    end
	end
  ch:sendTo("Carrying:\n\r")
  for objIter in ch:carrying() do
    ch:sendTo(objIter:getName().."\n\r")
    if(objIter:getType() == Object.Type.CONTAINER) then
  		ch:sendTo("\t\tis a container and it is ".. (objIter:isEmpty() and "empty" or "not empty") .. "\n\r")
		end
  end
  ch:sendTo("In the room with you:\n\r")
  for objIter in ch:getInRoom():objects() do
    ch:sendTo(objIter:getName().."\n\r")
    if(objIter:getType() == Object.Type.CONTAINER) then
      ch:sendTo("\t\tis a container and it is ".. (objIter:isEmpty() and "empty" or "not empty") .. "\n\r")
    end
  end
end
Command.registerCommand("luatest14",0,false,false,0,0,false,false,luatest14)
```

This endeavor required an unimaginable amount of continuous redesign on the C side.

# Rolling Planetgame

## Introduction
As requested by Advari and the imms in March of 2020. Coded to put control logic in the Lua layer. Adds a few features in that pursuit but it's mostly humdrum.

## How to use it
### Planet Flags
This introduces two planet flags, `rollenabled` and `rollactive`. 

`rollenabled` is a master flag that, if set, allows a planet to be part of the rolling capture system. If this flag is not set, the planet is ignored. Note, `nocapture` is still respected and if a planet is set to `nocapture` the presence of `rollenabled` is ignored. To enable a planet for the rolling planet game, set the `rollenabled` flag. Simple as that

`rollactive` is used internally and should not be set manually. It will be overwritten by the lua layer whenever it does its check, once a second at present. 

`captureplanet` requires the planet to not have the `nocapture` flag, and if it has the `rollenabled` flag, to have the `rollactive` flag. Any other combination (e.g. having `nocapture` or `rollenabled` but not `rollactive` will result in failure. The behavior if `rollactive` is set, but `rollenabled` is not, is undefined but practically means the planet can be captured so long as `nocapture` is not set.

### broadcasts
When the bits flip, that is, a planet goes from being available for capture to not or vice versa all connected players are shown a message indicating that the status has swapped.

### showplanet
Showplanet will include info on if a planet can be captured, for how long it will be possible to capture it, etc. That assumes it is enabled in the rolling capture game. if not, nothing will be printed out.

### settings in the code
The `planetgame.lua` file has some settings at the top which govern how frequently a planet can be captured, for how long, and if there is an offset between planets.

`everyX` in seconds, how often the window opens

`forY` in seconds, how long the window will be open for

`offsetPerPlanet` in seconds, how long the offset will be between multiple planets.

## Mechanics and notes
### State management
This is based off of the system clock and math there, so it does not matter if the mud crashes/resets/whatever, the state will reset to whatever it should be. You can't override this manually. The only other state involved is the flags set on planets, which can be managed through all the regular `setplanet` commands.

### lua internals
#### it's a program
This is a lua program, so it can be managed through the `lua` command if you have reason to unload it or reload it. If you unload it, the program will stop being invoked and it will leave things in whatever state they are in. If you want to prevent this from being loaded automatically, you can remove it from `autoload.lst` in the lua/src directory. `autoreload(true)` at the top means that if the script is crashed/unloaded for some reason it will automatically reload itself. the exception of course is if there is a syntax error that prevents it from being loaded in the first place. if it's not doing what you expect, do a `lua list` and make sure it is `resident.` If it isn't resident, call Miros maybe. Or, give it a `lua reload planetgame.lua` and see what comes out in the log.

#### it uses a timer
There is a timer registered to fire every second. This is what drives the thing and does the state changes and whatever. reading the code should be pretty clear in terms of what it does and how. Lua may seem a little strange if you are used to c, but trust me, there is way less code this way than there would be if we did it the other way, and it's easier to modify. Plus, I like working on the lua layer.

#### it uses high level interfaces
I had to add the flags functionality for planets but it is basically exactly the same model as is used for objects / rooms / etc. these operate through the proxy layer for safety, which you can read about in the general lotj lua manual.

#### new info trigger
Because folks really wanted to see this info in showplanet, I added a new mechanism for decorating existing things with info from lua modules. If you look at the code for showplanet, you will the following call nestled in there

```
char infostring[1024];
sprintf(infostring,"showplanet-%s",planet->name);
lua_trigger_on_ch_info(ch,infostring);
```

this invokes a callback/trigger in Lua which gives the program a chance to spit out some data to the player. The same pattern can be applied in other places.

# MCP-CPR Integration Documentation

## Overview

The CPR (Command Processing Router) system in LotJ provides a secure, authenticated RPC interface for external tools and AI agents to interact with the MUD. This document describes how the CPR system has been enhanced to support MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration with comprehensive, structured documentation.

## Architecture

### CPR System Components

1. **MQTT Transport**: CPR messages are sent/received via MQTT topics
   - Input: `in/cpr/*`
   - Output: `out/cpr/return/<call_id>` (success) or `out/cpr/error/<call_id>` (error)

2. **Authentication**: HMAC-SHA256 based authentication using account secrets
   - `CPR_AUTH_NONE`: No authentication required
   - `CPR_AUTH_OPTIONAL`: Authentication optional (enhanced features if authenticated)
   - `CPR_AUTH_REQUIRED`: Authentication mandatory

3. **Method Registry**: Up to 100 CPR methods can be registered with metadata

### Message Format

#### Request Envelope
```json
{
  "call_id": 12345,
  "signature": "<HMAC-SHA256 hex string>",
  "payload": "{\"account\":\"user\",\"method\":\"listMethods\",\"params\":{}}"
}
```

#### Response Format
```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": { /* method-specific response */ }
}
```

## MCP Documentation Structure

Each CPR method can include comprehensive MCP-compatible documentation:

### Documentation Fields

- **category**: High-level grouping (e.g., "world", "players", "monitoring")
- **subcategory**: Specific classification within category
- **readonly**: Boolean indicating if method modifies game state
- **description**: Detailed explanation for AI models
- **returns**: Description of return data structure
- **privacy**: Privacy implications and visibility rules
- **safety**: Safety considerations for state-modifying operations
- **requires_auth**: Whether authentication is required
- **use_cases**: Array of example use scenarios
- **limits**: Rate limits, pagination info
- **example**: Example parameters

## Discovering Available Methods

### Method: `listMethods`

**Authentication Required**: Yes (as of v2.0.0)

Returns all available CPR methods with their complete documentation.

#### Request
```json
{
  "account": "your_account",
  "method": "listMethods",
  "params": {}
}
```

#### Response Structure
```json
{
  "methods": [
    {
      "name": "methodName",
      "auth_level": "required|optional|none",
      "description": "Short description",
      "inputSchema": {
        /* JSON Schema for parameters */
      },
      "mcp": {
        /* Full MCP documentation object */
      }
    }
  ],
  "count": 21,
  "version": "2.0.0"
}
```

### Method: `getMethodDetails`

Get documentation for a specific method.

#### Request
```json
{
  "method": "getMethodDetails",
  "params": {
    "method": "listAreas"
  }
}
```

## Available Method Categories

### World Data (`category: "world"`)
- **listAreas**: List all game areas
- **getAreaDetails**: Detailed area information
- **listRooms**: List rooms with filtering
- **getRoomDetails**: Detailed room information

### Player Data (`category: "players"`)
- **listOnlinePlayers**: Currently connected players
- **getCharacterInfo**: Detailed character information (auth required)

### Game Data (`category: "game_data"`)
- **getSkillList**: Available skills and spells
- **searchHelp**: Search help documentation

### Monitoring (`category: "monitoring"`)
- **getServerStatus**: Server health and metrics
- **getRecentEvents**: Recent game events
- **sendLogEntry**: Add system log entries (auth required)

### Testing (`category: "testing"`)
- **executeCommand**: Execute commands as authenticated character (auth required)
- **runTestCommand**: Execute test commands (auth required)
- **validateArea**: Validate area files (auth required)
- **validateLprog**: Validate Lua programs (auth required)

### Development (`category: "development"`)
- **reloadArea**: Hot-reload areas (auth required)

### Communication (`category: "communication"`)
- **sendSystemMessage**: Broadcast announcements (auth required)

### Analytics (`category: "analytics"`)
- **getGameStatistics**: Comprehensive game statistics

## MCP Tool Generation

The CPR documentation is designed to be easily converted to MCP tool definitions:

### Example: Converting CPR Method to MCP Tool

#### CPR Documentation (from listMethods)
```json
{
  "name": "listAreas",
  "auth_level": "optional",
  "description": "List all game areas with basic information",
  "inputSchema": {
    "filter": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Optional filter by area name"
    }
  },
  "mcp": {
    "category": "world",
    "subcategory": "areas",
    "readonly": true,
    "description": "Returns a list of all game areas...",
    "returns": "Array of area objects..."
  }
}
```

#### Generated MCP Tool Definition
```typescript
{
  name: "lotj_listAreas",
  description: mcp.description,
  inputSchema: {
    type: "object",
    properties: inputSchema,
    required: []
  },
  metadata: {
    category: mcp.category,
    readonly: mcp.readonly,
    auth_required: (auth_level === "required")
  }
}
```

## Implementation Example

### Python MCP Server
```python
import json
import hashlib
import hmac
from typing import Dict, Any

class LotJCPRClient:
    def __init__(self, mqtt_client, account: str, secret: str):
        self.mqtt = mqtt_client
        self.account = account
        self.secret = secret
        self.call_id = 0
        
    def call_method(self, method: str, params: Dict[str, Any] = None) -> Dict:
        self.call_id += 1
        
        # Build payload
        payload = {
            "account": self.account,
            "method": method,
            "params": params or {}
        }
        payload_json = json.dumps(payload)
        
        # Generate signature
        signature = hmac.new(
            self.secret.encode(),
            payload_json.encode(),
            hashlib.sha256
        ).hexdigest()
        
        # Build envelope
        envelope = {
            "call_id": self.call_id,
            "signature": signature,
            "payload": payload_json
        }
        
        # Send via MQTT
        self.mqtt.publish("in/cpr", json.dumps(envelope))
        
        # Wait for response on out/cpr/return/{call_id}
        # or out/cpr/error/{call_id}
        return self.wait_for_response(self.call_id)

class LotJMCPServer:
    def __init__(self, cpr_client: LotJCPRClient):
        self.cpr = cpr_client
        self.tools = {}
        
    async def initialize(self):
        """Discover and register all CPR methods as MCP tools"""
        response = self.cpr.call_method("listMethods")
        
        for method in response["methods"]:
            tool = self.create_mcp_tool(method)
            self.tools[tool["name"]] = tool
            
    def create_mcp_tool(self, cpr_method: Dict) -> Dict:
        """Convert CPR method documentation to MCP tool"""
        return {
            "name": f"lotj_{cpr_method['name']}",
            "description": cpr_method.get("mcp", {}).get("description") 
                          or cpr_method["description"],
            "inputSchema": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": cpr_method.get("inputSchema", {}),
                "required": self.extract_required_params(cpr_method)
            },
            "handler": lambda params: self.cpr.call_method(
                cpr_method["name"], 
                params
            )
        }
```

## Security Considerations

1. **Authentication Required for Discovery**: `listMethods` requires authentication to prevent unauthorized enumeration of available methods.

2. **HMAC Signature Validation**: All authenticated methods verify HMAC-SHA256 signatures to ensure request integrity and authenticity.

3. **Account-Based Access Control**: Methods respect account permissions and visibility rules.

4. **Audit Logging**: All CPR calls are logged with account information and timestamps.

5. **Rate Limiting**: Consider implementing rate limits for resource-intensive operations.

## Best Practices

### For MCP Server Implementers

1. **Cache Method Documentation**: Call `listMethods` once at startup and cache the results.

2. **Respect Read-Only Flags**: Don't call methods marked `readonly: false` without user confirmation.

3. **Handle Authentication Levels**: 
   - Methods with `auth_level: "none"` can be called without authentication
   - Methods with `auth_level: "optional"` provide more data when authenticated
   - Methods with `auth_level: "required"` will fail without authentication

4. **Use Categories for Organization**: Group tools by category/subcategory for better UX.

5. **Implement Retry Logic**: Network failures should trigger retries with exponential backoff.

### For AI Agents

1. **Start with Read-Only Methods**: Begin exploration with safe, read-only methods.

2. **Respect Privacy Settings**: Some data is hidden based on authentication and visibility rules.

3. **Use Filtering and Pagination**: Many list methods support filtering to reduce data transfer.

4. **Batch Related Queries**: Minimize round-trips by planning query sequences.

5. **Monitor Rate Limits**: Respect any rate limits indicated in documentation.

## Testing

### Manual Testing with mosquitto_pub

```bash
# Prepare payload
PAYLOAD='{"account":"test","method":"listMethods","params":{}}'
SIGNATURE=$(echo -n "$PAYLOAD" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "your_secret" | cut -d' ' -f2)

# Create envelope
ENVELOPE=$(cat <<EOF
{
  "call_id": 1,
  "signature": "$SIGNATURE",
  "payload": "$PAYLOAD"
}
EOF
)

# Send via MQTT
mosquitto_pub -h localhost -t "in/cpr" -m "$ENVELOPE"

# Subscribe to responses
mosquitto_sub -h localhost -t "out/cpr/+/+" -v
```

### Automated Testing

```python
def test_cpr_documentation():
    """Verify all CPR methods have complete documentation"""
    client = LotJCPRClient(mqtt, "test_account", "test_secret")
    
    # Get all methods
    response = client.call_method("listMethods")
    
    for method in response["methods"]:
        assert "name" in method
        assert "auth_level" in method
        assert "description" in method
        
        if "mcp" in method:
            mcp = method["mcp"]
            assert "category" in mcp
            assert "description" in mcp
            assert "readonly" in mcp
            
        # Test that method can be called (if accessible)
        if method["auth_level"] != "required":
            details = client.call_method("getMethodDetails", {
                "method": method["name"]
            })
            assert details["name"] == method["name"]
```

    single user.  This should be called when the descriptor is initialised.
*/
protocol_t* ProtocolCreate( void );

/*  Function: ProtocolDestroy

    Frees the memory allocated by the specified structure.  This should be
    called just before a descriptor is freed.
*/
void ProtocolDestroy( protocol_t* apProtocol );

/*  Function: ProtocolNegotiate

    Negatiates with the client to see which protocols the user supports, and
    stores the results in the user's protocol structure.  Call this when you
    wish to perform negotiation (but only call it once).  It is usually called
    either immediately after the user has connected, or just after they have
    entered the game.
*/
void ProtocolNegotiate( descriptor_t* apDescriptor );
/*  Function: ProtocolNoEcho

    Tells the client to switch echo on or off.
*/
void ProtocolNoEcho( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, bool abOn );
/*  Function: ProtocolInput

    Extracts any negotiation sequences from the input buffer, and passes back
    whatever is left for the mud to parse normally.  Call this after data has
    been read into the input buffer, before it is used for anything else.
*/
void ProtocolInput( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, char* apData, int aSize, char* apOut );

/*  Function: ProtocolOutput

    This function takes a string, applies colour codes to it, and returns the
    result.  It should be called just before writing to the output buffer.

    The special character used to indicate the start of a colour sequence is
    '\t' (i.e., a tab, or ASCII character 9).  This makes it easy to include
    in help files (as you can literally press the tab key) as well as strings
    (where you can use \t instead).  However players can't send tabs (on most
    muds at least), so this stops them from sending colour codes to each other.

    The predefined colours are:

     n: no colour (switches colour off)

     r: dark red                        R: light red
     g: dark green                      G: light green
     b: dark blue                       B: light blue
     y: dark yellow                     Y: light yellow
     m: dark magenta                    M: light magenta
     c: dark cyan                       C: light cyan
     w: dark white                      W: light white

     a: dark azure                      A: light azure
     j: dark jade                       J: light jade
     l: dark lime                       L: light lime
     o: dark orange                     O: bright orange
     p: dark pink                       P: light pink
     t: dark tan                        T: light tan
     v: dark violet                     V: light violet

    So for example "This is \tOorange\tn." will colour the word "orange".  You
    can add more colours yourself just by updating the switch statement.

    It's also possible to explicitly specify an RGB value, by including the four
    character colour sequence (as used by ColourRGB) within square brackets, eg:

      This is a \t[F010]very dark green foreground\tn.

    The square brackets can also be used to send unicode characters, like this:

      Boat: \t[U9973/B]
      Rook: \t[U9814/C]

    For example you might use 'B' to represent a boat on your ASCII map, or a 'C'
    to represent a castle - but players with UTF-8 support would actually see the
    appropriate unicode characters for a boat or a rook (the chess playing piece).

    The exact syntax is '\t' (tab), '[', 'U' (indicating unicode), then the decimal
    number of the unicode character (see http://www.unicode.org/charts), then '/'
    followed by the ASCII character/s that should be used if the client doesn't
    support UTF-8.  The ASCII sequence can be up to 7 characters in length, but in
    most cases you'll only want it to be one or two characters (so that it has the
    same alignment as the unicode character).

    Finally, this function also allows you to embed MXP tags.  The easiest and
    safest way to do this is via the ( and ) bracket options:

      From here, you can walk \t(north\t).

    However it's also possible to include more explicit MSP tags, like this:

      The baker offers to sell you a \t<send href="buy pie">pie\t</send>.

    Note that the MXP tags will automatically be removed if the user doesn't
    support MXP, but it's very important you remember to close the tags.
*/
const char* ProtocolOutput( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, const char* apData, int* apLength );

/******************************************************************************
    Copyover save/load functions.
 ******************************************************************************/

/*  Function: CopyoverGet

    Returns the protocol values stored as a short string.  If your mud uses
    copyover, you should call this for each player and insert it after their
    name in the temporary text file.
*/
const char* CopyoverGet( descriptor_t* apDescriptor );

/*  Function: CopyoverSet

    Call this function for each player after a copyover, passing in the string
    you added to the temporary text file.  This will restore their protocol
    settings, and automatically renegotiate MSDP/ATCP.

    Note that the client doesn't recognise a copyover, and therefore refuses to
    renegotiate certain telnet options (to avoid loops), so they really need to
    be saved.  However MSDP/ATCP is handled through scripts, and we don't want
    to have to save all of the REPORT variables, so it's easier to renegotiate.

    Client name and version are not saved.  It is recommended you save these in
    the player file, as then you can grep to collect client usage stats.
*/
void CopyoverSet( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, const char* apData );

/******************************************************************************
    MSDP functions.
 ******************************************************************************/

/*  Function: MSDPUpdate

    Call this regularly (I'd suggest at least once per second) to flush every
    dirty MSDP variable that has been requested by the client via REPORT.  This
    will automatically use ATCP instead if MSDP is not supported by the client.
*/
void MSDPUpdate( descriptor_t* apDescriptor );

/*  Function: MSDPFlush

    Works like MSDPUpdate(), except only flushes a specific variable.  The
    variable will only actually be sent if it's both reported and dirty.

    Call this function after setting a variable if you want it to be reported
    immediately, instead of on the next update.
*/
void MSDPFlush( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, variable_t aMSDP );

/*  Function: MSDPSend

    Send the specified MSDP variable to the player.  You shouldn't ever really
    need to do this manually, except perhaps when debugging something.  This
    will automatically use ATCP instead if MSDP is not supported by the client.
*/
void MSDPSend( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, variable_t aMSDP );

/*  Function: MSDPSendPair

    Send the specified strings to the user as an MSDP variable/value pair.  This
    will automatically use ATCP instead if MSDP is not supported by the client.
*/
void MSDPSendPair( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, const char* apVariable, const char* apValue );

/*  Function: MSDPSendList

    Works like MSDPSendPair, but the value is sent as an MSDP array.

    apValue should be a list of values separated by spaces.
*/
void MSDPSendList( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, const char* apVariable, const char* apValue );

/*  Function: MSDPSetNumber

    Call this whenever an MSDP integer variable has changed.  The easiest
    approach is to send every MSDP variable within an update function (and
    this is what the snippet does by default), but if the variable is only
    set in one place you can just move its MDSPSend() call to there.

    You can also this function for bools, chars, enums, short ints, etc.
*/
void MSDPSetNumber( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, variable_t aMSDP, int aValue );

/*  Function: MSDPSetString

    Call this whenever an MSDP string variable has changed.  The easiest
    approach is to send every MSDP variable within an update function (and
    this is what the snippet does by default), but if the variable is only
    set in one place you can just move its MDSPSend() call to there.
*/
void MSDPSetString( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, variable_t aMSDP, const char* apValue );

/*  Function: MSDPSetTable

    Works like MSDPSetString, but the value is sent as an MSDP table.

    You must add the MSDP_VAR and MSDP_VAL manually, for example:

    snprintf( Buffer, sizeof( Buffer ), "%c%s%c%s", (char)MSDP_VAR, Name, (char)MSDP_VAL, Value );
    MSDPSetTable( d, eMSDP_TEST, Buffer );
*/
void MSDPSetTable( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, variable_t aMSDP, const char* apValue );

/*  Function: MSDPSetArray

    Works like MSDPSetString, but the value is sent as an MSDP array.

    You must add the MSDP_VAR before each element manually, for example:

    snprintf( Buffer, sizeof( Buffer ), "%c%s%c%s", (char)MSDP_VAL, Val1, (char)MSDP_VAL, Val2 );
    MSDPSetArray( d, eMSDP_TEST, Buffer );
*/
void MSDPSetArray( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, variable_t aMSDP, const char* apValue );

/******************************************************************************
    MSSP functions.
 ******************************************************************************/

/*  Function: MSSPSetPlayers

    Stores the current number of players.  The first time it's called, it also
    stores the uptime.
*/
void MSSPSetPlayers( int aPlayers );

/******************************************************************************
    MXP functions.
 ******************************************************************************/

/*  Function: MXPCreateTag

    Puts the specified tag into a secure line, if MXP is supported.  If the user
    doesn't support MXP they will see the string unchanged, meaning they will
    see the <send> tags or whatever.  You should therefore check for support and
    provide a different sequence for other users, or better yet just embed MXP
    tags for the ProtocolOutput() function.
*/
const char* MXPCreateTag( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, const char* apTag );

/*  Function: MXPSendTag

    This works like MXPCreateTag, but instead of returning the string it sends
    it directly to the user.  This is mainly useful for the <VERSION> tag.
*/
void MXPSendTag( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, const char* apTag );

/******************************************************************************
    Sound functions.
 ******************************************************************************/

/*  Function: SoundSend

    Sends the specified sound trigger to the player, using MSDP or ATCP if
    supported, MSP if not.  The trigger string itself is a relative path and
    filename, eg: SoundSend( pDesc, "monster/growl.wav" );
*/
void SoundSend( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, const char* apTrigger );

/******************************************************************************
    Colour functions.
 ******************************************************************************/

/*  Function: ColourRGB

    Returns a colour as an escape code, based on the RGB value provided.  The
    string must be four characters, where the first is either 'f' for foreground
    or 'b' for background (case insensitive), and the other three characters are
    numeric digits in the range 0 to 5, representing red, green and blue.

    For example "F500" returns a red foreground, "B530" an orange background,
    and so on.  An invalid colour will clear whatever you've set previously.

    If the user doesn't support XTerm 256 colours, this function will return the
    best-fit ANSI colour instead.

    If you wish to embed colours in strings, use ProtocolOutput().
*/
const char* ColourRGB( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, const char* apRGB );

/******************************************************************************
    Unicode (UTF-8 conversion) functions.
 ******************************************************************************/

/*  Function: UnicodeGet

    Returns the UTF-8 sequence for the specified unicode value.
*/
char* UnicodeGet( int aValue );

/*  Function: UnicodeAdd

    Adds the UTF-8 sequence for the specified unicode value onto the end of the
    string, without adding a NUL character at the end.
*/
void UnicodeAdd( char** apString, int aValue );

/*************** START GMCP ***************/
extern const char GoAheadStr[];
extern const char iac_sb_gmcp[];
extern const char iac_se[];
extern void SendUpdatedGMCP( descriptor_t* apDescriptor );
extern void UpdateGMCPNull( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, GMCP_VARIABLE var );
extern void UpdateGMCPString( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, GMCP_VARIABLE var, const char* string );
extern void UpdateGMCPNumber( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, GMCP_VARIABLE var, const long long number );
extern void UpdateGMCPBoolean( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, GMCP_VARIABLE var, const bool value );
extern void UpdateGMCPObject( descriptor_t* apDescriptor, GMCP_VARIABLE var, const char* json );
extern void sendMudletGUIInfo( descriptor_t* d );
/*************** END GMCP ***************/

#endif /* PROTOCOL_H */

version: '3.9'
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16.3
    restart: always
    hostname: db
    expose: 
      - '5432'
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: root
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: 12345
      POSTGRES_DB: lotj
      DATABASE_NAME: lotj
      DATABASE_DB: lotj
      POSTGRES_DATABASE: lotj
    ports:
      - '5432:5432'
    networks:
      - mud_network
    volumes: 
      - ./migrations/db/:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d #need to fix for postgres
  mud:
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true
    build: 
      context: .
      args:
        NOT_PRODUCTION: 1
        MEMORY_DEBUG: 1
        PROFILE: 1
    depends_on:
     - db
     - mosquitto
     - rpcsidecar
     - discord2mqtt
    environment:
      - VALGRIND=${VALGRIND:-}
      - NOGDB=${NOGDB:-}
      - NOT_PRODUCTION=TRUE
      - GMON_OUT_PREFIX=/opt/lotj/log/gmon
      - FULL_DEBUG=${FULL_DEBUG:-}
      - GDBSERVER=${GDBSERVER:-}
      - RAILS_ENV=development
      - DATABASE_HOST=db
      - DATABASE_PORT=5432
      - DATABASE_USER=root
      - DATABASE_PASSWORD=12345
      - DATABASE_NAME=lotj
      - DATABASE_DB=lotj
      - ENABLE_LPROGS=${ENABLE_LPROGS:-}
      - FASTBOOT=${FASTBOOT:-}
      - LPROGS_DISABLED=${LPROGS_DISABLED:-}
      - ASAN_OPTIONS=${ASAN_OPTIONS:-}halt_on_error=0
      - EXE_FILE=../src/swreality
      - EXEC=swreality
    security_opt:
      - seccomp:unconfined
    ports:
      - '5656:5656'
      - '5666:5666'
      - '4444:4444'
    networks:
      - mud_network
    volumes:
      - ./src/lua:/opt/lotj/src/lua
      - ./backtraces:/opt/lotj/backtraces
      - ./log:/opt/lotj/log
      - ./system:/opt/lotj/system
      - ./rocksdbs:/opt/lotj/rocksdbs
      - ./looms:/opt/lotj/looms
      - ./data:/opt/lotj/data
      - ./.dbc.d:/opt/lotj/system/dbc.d
  lotjwebbuffer:
    depends_on:
      - mud
      - db
    build: ./webbuffer/
    restart: "no"
    networks:
      - mud_network
    ports: 
      - '3001:3001'
    environment:
      - PORT=3001
      - FIREHOSE_HOST=mud
      - FIREHOSE_PORT=5666
      - DATABASE_HOST=db
      - DATABASE_PORT=5432
      - DATABASE_USER=root
      - DATABASE_PASSWORD=12345
      - DATABASE_DB=lotj
      - DATABASE_NAME=lotj
      - DATABASE_DIALECT=postgresql
      - DATABASE_POOLMAX=5
      - DATABASE_POOLMIN=0
      - DATABASE_POOLACQ=30000
      - DATABASE_POOLIDLE=10000
      - DATABASE_SSL=false  
  rpcsidecar:
    build: ./rpcsidecar
    ports:
      - '3000:3000'
    environment:
      - MQTT_SERVER=mosquitto
      - MQTT_PORT=1883
      - OPENAI_API_KEY=${OPENAI_API_KEY:-}
      - OPENAI_ORG=${OPENAI_ORG:-}
      - GHAUTH=${GHAUTH:-}
      - SMTPUSER=${SMTPUSER:-}
      - SMTPPASSWORD=${SMTPPASSWORD:-}
      - SMTPSERVER=${SMTPSERVER:-}
      - SMTPPORT=${SMTPPORT:-}
      - MAILJET_API_KEY=${MAILJET_API_KEY:-}
      - MAILJET_SECRET_KEY=${MAILJET_SECRET_KEY:-}
      - PORT=3000
    depends_on:
      - mosquitto
    networks:
      - mud_network
    restart: on-failure

  discord2mqtt:
    build: ./discord2mqtt
    environment:
      - MQTT_SERVER=mosquitto
      - MQTT_PORT=1883
      - DISCORD_TOKEN=${DISCORD_TOKEN:-}
    depends_on:
      - mosquitto
    networks:
      - mud_network
    restart: on-failure
  mosquitto:
    image: eclipse-mosquitto:latest
    container_name: mosquitto
    ports:
      - "1883:1883"
      - "9001:9001"
    volumes:
      - ./mosquitto/config:/mosquitto/config
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - mud_network
    
  nginx:
    image: nginx:1.17.8
    ports:
      - '80:80'
      - '443:443'
    networks:
      - mud_network
    volumes:
      - ./www/nginx:/etc/nginx/conf.d
      - ./www/logs/nginx:/var/log/nginx
      - ./www/wordpress:/var/www/html
    depends_on:
      - wordpress
    restart: always
    profiles: 
      - website
  
  mysql:
    image: mysql:8.3.0
    hostname: mysql
    expose: 
      - '3306'
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: '12345'
    ports:
      - '3306:3306'
    networks:
      - mud_network
    volumes: 
      - ./mysql/:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d
    command: '--authentication_policy=CACHING_SHA2_PASSWORD --sql_mode=ALLOW_INVALID_DATES'
    profiles: 
      - website
  wordpress:
    image: wordpress:php8.2-fpm
    volumes:
      - ./wwwconfig/php.conf.ini:/usr/local/etc/php/conf.d/conf.ini
      - ./www/wordpress:/var/www/html
      - ./src:/home/lotj/LotJ/src
      - ./system:/home/lotj/LotJ/system
    ports:
      - '9000:9000'
    networks:
      - mud_network
    environment:
      - WORDPRESS_DB_NAME=lotjwp
      - WORDPRESS_TABLE_PREFIX=wp_
      - WORDPRESS_DB_HOST=db
      - WORDPRESS_DB_USER=root
      - WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD=12345
    depends_on:
      - mysql
    restart: always
    profiles:
      - website
networks:
  mud_network:
    driver: bridge

FROM ubuntu:24.04

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive 

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --allow-downgrades make gcc \
                       liblua5.4 libcurl4-openssl-dev gdb valgrind \
                       libc6-dbg libsystemd0 libsystemd-dev libb64-dev \
                       curl liboath-dev tzdata ca-certificates gnupg \
                       locales gdbserver libb2-dev g++ libmosquitto-dev \
                       libsource-highlight-dev ruby ruby-dev lsb-release \
                       libyaml-dev libcjson-dev zlib1g zlib1g-dev python3 \
                       python3-pip python3-venv graphviz libasan8 libssl-dev

# Something about UTF8 locale?
RUN sed -i '/en_US.UTF-8/s/^# //g' /etc/locale.gen && locale-gen
ENV LC_ALL en_US.UTF-8     

RUN mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings

# Install postgres client
RUN curl -fsSL https://www.postgresql.org/media/keys/ACCC4CF8.asc | gpg --dearmor | tee /usr/share/keyrings/postgresql-archive-keyring.gpg >/dev/null
RUN echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/postgresql-archive-keyring.gpg] http://apt.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt $(lsb_release -cs)-pgdg main" | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/postgresql.list
RUN apt-get update && apt-get -y install postgresql-client-16 libpq-dev

# Create and activate a virtual environment
RUN python3 -m venv /opt/venv

# Install gprof2dot in the virtual environment
RUN /opt/venv/bin/pip install gprof2dot

# Update PATH environment variable
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"

RUN mkdir /opt/lotj

# Move DB migrations into the container and set up activerecord ruby tool
COPY migrations /opt/lotj/migrations
WORKDIR /opt/lotj/migrations
RUN gem install bundler
RUN bundle config --global silence_root_warning 1 
RUN bundle update
RUN bundle install

RUN mv db/config.yml.example db/config.yml

# Copy source into container and build the mud
COPY src /opt/lotj/src
RUN mkdir /opt/lotj/src/o
WORKDIR /opt/lotj/src

ARG NOT_PRODUCTION
ARG PROFILE
ARG MEMORY_DEBUG
ENV NOT_PRODUCTION ${NOT_PRODUCTION}
ENV PROFILE ${PROFILE}
ENV MEMORY_DEBUG ${MEMORY_DEBUG}

RUN make -j16

# Start the game (must be in the area dir)
WORKDIR /opt/lotj/system
EXPOSE 5656
RUN echo "set print thread-events off" >> /root/.gdbinit
RUN echo "set print inferior-events off" >> /root/.gdbinit
RUN echo "handle SIGTERM pass" >> /root/.gdbinit
ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/lotj/src/wait-for-postgres.sh"]
CMD ["/opt/lotj/src/wait-for-it.sh", "db:5432", "--", "/opt/lotj/src/run_under_docker.sh","/opt/lotj/src/swreality","5656"]

# Comment out the above CMD and uncomment this one to make an interactive instance of the mud's container.
# You can then run commands in it using "docker-compose exec mud bash", like "./run-gdb 5656"
# CMD ["tail", "-f", "/dev/null"]

CC      = gcc
CXX     = g++      # For the cpp modules 
ifdef MEMORY_DEBUG
  FSANITIZE = -fsanitize=address
  $(info Memory Debugging build enabled)
endif
ifdef PROFILE
  PROF = -pg
  $(info Profiling build enabled)
endif
#Uncomment the next line if you want request support
#DBUGFLG = -DREQUESTS
DEBUG   = -DDEBUG -ggdb
DEFINES = -DCLIENT
ifdef NOT_PRODUCTION
	NOTPROD = -DNOT_PRODUCTION
endif

C_FLAGS = -fsigned-char -g3 -W -Wall $(PROF) $(NOCRYPT) $(DBUGFLG) $(DEBUG) $(NOTPROD) -export-dynamic $(DEFINES) $(FSANITIZE)
W_FLAGS = -pedantic -W -Wall -Wformat-security -Winline -Wstrict-prototypes -Wshadow -Wpointer-arith -Wcast-align -Wcast-qual -Wredundant-decls

char* old_flag_string( int bitvector, char* const flagarray[] )
{
    static char buf[MSL];
    int x;
    buf[0] = '\0';

    for ( x = 0; x < 32 ; x++ )
        if ( IS_SET( bitvector, 1 << x ) )
        {
            strlcat( buf, flagarray[x], MSL );

            /* don't catenate a blank if the last char is blank  --Gorog */
            if ( buf[0] != '\0' && ' ' != buf[strlen( buf ) - 1] )
                strlcat( buf, " ", MSL );
        }

    if ( ( x = strlen( buf ) ) > 0 )
        buf[--x] = '\0';

    return buf;
}

char* flag_string( EXT_BV* bitvector, const FLAG_INFO* flags )
{
    static char buf[MSL];
    buf[0] = '\0';
    for ( int i = 0; flags[i].flag != LAST_FLAG_VALUE; i++ )
    {
        if ( xIS_SET( *bitvector, flags[i].flag ) )
        {
            if ( strlen(buf) > 0 )
                strlcat( buf, " ", MSL );
            if ( NULLSTR( flags[i].name ) )
                strlcat( buf, "BUG:UNNAMED_FLAG", MSL );
            else
                strlcat( buf, flags[i].name, MSL );
        }
    }
    return buf;
}

// Use this when we need to print set flags from an old-school bitvector stored as an int.

// A set handler for editing flags
// Takes the current EXT_BV value from the entity and the list of flags given as an argument.
// If the list of flags given is empty, prints the list of possible flags.
// Supports args as: +flagname (set to true), -flagname (set to false), or flagname (toggle)
//
// Standard behavior:
// mob->flags = set_flags( ch, actflags, mob->flags, arg, true );
// 
// Custom flag changing behavior:
// EXT_BV new_flags = set_flags( ch, actflags, mob->flags, arg, false );
// if ( xIS_SET( mob->flags, ACT_NPC ) != xIS_SET( new_flags, ACT_NPC ) ) {
//   ch_println( ch, "Can't change the NPC flag" );
//   return;    
// }
// print_flags_set_results( ch, actflags, mob->flags, new_flags );
// mob->flags = new_flags;
//
EXT_BV set_flags(
    CHAR_DATA* ch,
    const FLAG_INFO* flags,
    EXT_BV current_value,
    const char* argument,
    bool print_results
) {
    static char arg_part[MIL];
    EXT_BV result = current_value;
    if ( NULLSTR( argument ) )
    {
        ch_printf( ch, "&zCurrent value: &C" );
        ch_println( ch, flag_string( &current_value, flags ) );
        ch_println( ch, "" );
        ch_println( ch, "&zAvailable options:" );
        ch_println( ch, flag_options_descs( flags ) );
        return result;
    }
    while ( !NULLSTR( argument ) )
    {
        argument = one_argument( argument, arg_part );
        char* flagname = arg_part;
        bool force_true = false;
        bool force_false = false;

        if ( !str_prefix( "+", flagname ) )
        {
            force_true = true;
            flagname++;
        }
        else if ( !str_prefix( "-", flagname ) )
        {
            force_false = true;
            flagname++;
        }

        const FLAG_INFO* flag = flag_from_name( flags, flagname );
        if ( !flag )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "&zUnknown flag:&C %s", flagname );
        }
        else
        {
            if ( force_true )
                xSET_BIT( result, flag->flag );
            else if ( force_false )
                xREMOVE_BIT( result, flag->flag );
            else
                xTOGGLE_BIT( result, flag->flag );
        }
    }
    if ( print_results )
        print_flags_set_results( ch, flags, current_value, result );
    return result;
}

// Call this to print the results of setting flags. Can be called automatically by apply_flags_set
// if print_results is passed as true, or done separately after custom flag changing logic.
void print_flags_set_results( CHAR_DATA* ch, const FLAG_INFO* flags, EXT_BV prev, EXT_BV new )
{
    if ( xSAME_BITS( prev, new ) )
    {
        ch_println( ch, "&zNo flags changed.");
        return;
    }

    for ( int i = 0; flags[i].flag != LAST_FLAG_VALUE; i++ )
    {
        bool prev_value = xIS_SET( prev, flags[i].flag );
        bool new_value = xIS_SET( new, flags[i].flag );
        if ( prev_value != new_value )
            ch_println( ch, "&C%s &zset from &C%s &zto &C%s", flags[i].name,
                prev_value ? "true" : "false",
                new_value ? "true" : "false" );
    }
}

char* flag_options_string( char* const flagarray[], int range )
{
    static char buf[MSL];
    buf[0] = '\0';
    strlcat( buf, "&B", MSL );
    char* sort_flagarray[range];

    for ( int x = 0; x < range; x++ )
        sort_flagarray[x] = flagarray[x];

    qsort( &sort_flagarray[0], range, sizeof( char* ), ( int ( * )( const void*, const void* ) )compare_strings );
    int line_len = 0;
    bool main_color = true;

    for ( int x = 0; x < range; x++ )
    {
        if ( NULLSTR( sort_flagarray[x] ) )
            continue;

        if ( line_len + 1 + strlen( sort_flagarray[x] ) > 80 )
        {
            strlcat( buf, "\n", MSL );
            strlcat( buf, main_color ? "&037" : "&116", MSL );
            strlcat( buf, sort_flagarray[x], MSL );
            line_len = strlen( sort_flagarray[x] );
        }
        else
        {
            if ( line_len > 0 )
            {
                strlcat( buf, " ", MSL );
                line_len += 1;
            }

            strlcat( buf, main_color ? "&037" : "&116", MSL );
            strlcat( buf, sort_flagarray[x], MSL );
            line_len += strlen( sort_flagarray[x] );
        }

        main_color = !main_color;
    }

    strlcat( buf, "\n", MSL );
    return buf;
}

char* flag_options_descs( const FLAG_INFO* flags )
{
    static char buf[MSL];
    strlcpy( buf, "", MSL );
    int name_len_a = 0, name_len_b = 0, desc_len_a = 0, desc_len_b = 0, desc_len = 0;
    
    int flag_count = 0;
    for ( int i = 0; flags[i].flag != LAST_FLAG_VALUE; i++ )
        flag_count++;

    // Create an array local to the function
    FLAG_INFO arr[flag_count];
    
    // Copy the contents of the source array into it
    for ( int i = 0; i < flag_count; i++ )
        arr[i] = flags[i];

    // Alphabetize it
    qsort( &arr, flag_count, sizeof( FLAG_INFO ), ( int( * )( const void*, const void* ) ) compare_flags );

    int i = 0;
    int x = ceil( ( (double) flag_count ) / 2 );
    int y = x;

    // Find the length of the longest flag name
    while ( i < y )
    {
        if ( (int) strlen( arr[i].name ) > name_len_a )
            name_len_a = strlen( arr[i].name );
        
        if ( x < flag_count && (int) strlen( arr[x].name ) > name_len_b )
            name_len_b = strlen( arr[x].name );

        if ( (int) strlen( arr[i].desc ) > desc_len_a )
            desc_len_a = strlen( arr[i].desc );

        if ( x < flag_count && (int) strlen( arr[x].desc ) > desc_len_b )
            desc_len_b = strlen( arr[x].desc );

        i++;
        x++;
    }

    // The maximum description length should be able to fit into 80 characters with all the other contents
    // Minimum of 11 in case descriptions are empty
    desc_len = (int) ( ( 80 - 9 - ( name_len_a + name_len_b ) ) / 2 );
    desc_len_a = URANGE( 11, desc_len_a, desc_len );
    desc_len_b = URANGE( 11, desc_len_b, desc_len );
    
    // Print the header and spacer
    snprintf( buf, MSL, "&z%*s &w| &z%-*s &z| &z%*s &w| &z%-*s\n", name_len_a, "Name", desc_len_a, "Description", name_len_b, "Name", desc_len, "Description" );
    snprintf( buf + strlen( buf ), MSL - strlen( buf ),
    "&z%.*s\n", (name_len_a + name_len_b + desc_len_a + desc_len_b + 9), "--------------------------------------------------------------------------------" );
    
    bool color_var = false;
    i = 0;
    x = ceil( ( (double) flag_count ) / 2 );
    y = x;

    // Iterate through the list, crafting two alphabetized columns with alternating row colors into a single string.
    while ( i < y )
    {
        snprintf( buf + strlen( buf ), MSL - strlen( buf ), "%s%*s &w| %s%-*s", color_var ? "&037" : "&116", name_len_a, arr[i].name, color_var ? "&037" : "&116", desc_len_a, truncate_string( arr[i].desc, desc_len_a ) );
        if ( x < flag_count )
            snprintf( buf + strlen( buf ), MSL - strlen( buf ), " &z| %s%*s &w| %s%-*s\n", color_var ? "&037" : "&116", name_len_b, arr[x].name, color_var ? "&037" : "&116", desc_len_b, truncate_string( arr[x].desc, desc_len_b ) );
        else
            snprintf( buf + strlen( buf ), MSL - strlen( buf ), "\n" );
        
        color_var = !color_var;   
        i++;
        x++;
    }

    // Returns the completed string
    return buf;
}

/*
    Changes carriage returns into <br> for HTML
    Changes spaces into ' '
*/
char* conv_tag( char* str )
{
    static char newstr[MSL];
    int i, j;
    int itag = 0;

    for ( i = j = 0; str[i] != '\0'; i++ )
    {
        if ( str[i] == '\n' )
        {
            newstr[j++] = '<';
            newstr[j++] = 'b';
            newstr[j++] = 'r';
            newstr[j++] = '>';
        }
        else if ( str[i] == '<' )
        {
            itag++;
            newstr[j++] = str[i];
        }
        else if ( str[i] == '>' )
        {
            itag--;
            newstr[j++] = str[i];
        }
        else if ( str[i] == ' ' )
        {
            if ( itag <= 0 )
            {
                newstr[j++] = '&';
                newstr[j++] = 'n';
                newstr[j++] = 'b';
                newstr[j++] = 's';
                newstr[j++] = 'p';
                newstr[j++] = ';';
            }
            else
            {
                newstr[j++] = str[i];
            }
        }
        else if ( str[i] != '\r' )
        {
            newstr[j++] = str[i];
        }
    }

    newstr[j] = '\0';
    return newstr;
}

/*
    Changes spaces into %20 for URL Addresses
*/
char* convert_sp( char* str )
{
    static char newstr[MSL];
    int i, j;

    for ( i = j = 0; str[i] != '\0'; i++ )
        if ( str[i] != ' ' )
        {
            newstr[j++] = str[i];
        }
        else
        {
            newstr[j++] = '%';
            newstr[j++] = '2';
            newstr[j++] = '0';
        }

    newstr[j] = '\0';
    return newstr;
}

CMDF do_goto( CHAR_DATA* ch, char* argument )
{
    char arg[MIL];
    ROOM_INDEX_DATA* location;
    CHAR_DATA* fch;
    CHAR_DATA* fch_next;
    ROOM_INDEX_DATA* in_room;
    AREA_DATA* pArea;
    int vnum;
    one_argument( argument, arg );

    if ( NULLSTR( arg ) )
    {
        ch_println( ch, "Goto where?" );
        return;
    }

    if ( !is_number( arg ) && ( fch = get_char_world_full( ch, arg ) ) )
    {
        if ( !IS_NPC( fch ) && get_trust( ch ) < get_trust( fch ) && has_pcflag( fch, PCFLAG_DND ) )
        {
            pager_printf( ch,
                          "Sorry. %s does not wish to be disturbed.\n", fch->name );
            pager_printf( fch, "Your DND flag just foiled %s's goto command.\n", ch->name );
            return;
        }
    }

    if ( ( location = find_location( ch, arg ) ) == NULL )
    {
        if ( !is_number( arg ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "No such location." );
            return;
        }

        vnum = atoi( arg );

        if ( !is_valid_vnum( vnum ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "&RSorry, %d IS NOT a valid vnum!", vnum );
            return;
        }

        if ( vnum < 0 )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "You cannot find that..." );
            return;
        }

        pArea = area_from_vnum( vnum );
        
        if ( !pArea )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "That vnum is not withint the range of a valid area." );
            return;
        }

        if ( !can_build( ch, pArea ) )
            return;

        location = make_room( vnum, TRUE );

        if ( !location )
        {
            bug( "Goto: make_room failed", 0 );
            return;
        }

        set_char_color( AT_WHITE, ch );
        ch_println( ch, "Waving your hand, you form order from swirling chaos,\nand step into a new reality..." );
    }

    if ( room_is_private( ch, location ) )
    {
        if ( get_trust( ch ) < sysdata.level_override_private )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "That room is private right now." );
            return;
        }
        else
            ch_println( ch, "Overriding private flag!" );
    }

    if ( xIS_SET( location->flags, ROOM_ADMIN ) && get_trust( ch ) < 105 )
    {
        ch_println( ch, "You aren't allowed into administrative rooms unless invited." );
        return;
    }


    
    if ( !can_build( ch, location->area ) )
        return;

    in_room = ch->in_room;

    if ( ch->fighting )
        stop_fighting( ch, TRUE );

    if ( !has_pcflag( ch, PCFLAG_WIZINVIS ) )
    {
        if ( ch->pcdata && ch->pcdata->bamfout[0] != '\0' )
            act( AT_IMMORT, "$T", ch, NULL, ch->pcdata->bamfout,  TO_ROOM );
        else
            act( AT_IMMORT, "$n $T", ch, NULL, "leaves in a swirl of the force.",  TO_ROOM );
    }

    ch->regoto = ch->in_room->vnum;
    char_from_room( ch );

    if ( ch->mount )
    {
        char_from_room( ch->mount );
        char_to_room( ch->mount, location );
    }

    if ( ch->carrying )
    {
        char_from_room( ch->carrying );
        char_to_room( ch->carrying, location );
    }

    char_to_room( ch, location );

    if ( !has_pcflag( ch, PCFLAG_WIZINVIS ) )
    {
        if ( ch->pcdata && ch->pcdata->bamfin[0] != '\0' )
            act( AT_IMMORT, "$T", ch, NULL, ch->pcdata->bamfin,  TO_ROOM );
        else
            act( AT_IMMORT, "$n $T", ch, NULL, "enters in a swirl of the force.",  TO_ROOM );
    }

    do_look( ch, "auto" );

    if ( ch->in_room == in_room )
        return;

    for ( fch = in_room->first_person; fch; fch = fch_next )
    {
        fch_next = fch->next_in_room;

        if ( fch->master == ch && IS_IMMORTAL( fch ) )
        {
            act( AT_ACTION, "You follow $N.", fch, NULL, ch, TO_CHAR );
            do_goto( fch, argument );
        }
        /* Experimental change by Gorog so imm's personal mobs follow them */
        else if ( IS_NPC( fch ) && fch->master == ch )
        {
            char_from_room ( fch );
            char_to_room( fch, location );
        }
    }

    return;
}

CMDF do_rgoto( CHAR_DATA* ch, char* argument )
{
    char arg1[MIL];
    char arg2[MIL];
    int vnum;
    int vnum1;
    int vnum2;
    AREA_DATA* pArea, *pArea2;
    char buf[MSL];
    one_argument( argument, arg1 );
    one_argument( argument, arg2 );

    if ( arg1[0] == '\0' || arg2[0] == '\0' || !is_number( arg1 ) || !is_number( arg2 ) || atoi( arg1 ) >= atoi( arg2 ) )
    {
        ch_println( ch, "&zSyntax: &Crgoto <&wfirstvnum&C> <&wlastvnum&C>?" );
        return;
    }

    vnum1 = atoi( arg1 );
    vnum2 = atoi( arg2 );

    pArea = area_from_vnum( vnum1 );
    pArea2 = area_from_vnum( vnum2 );

    if ( !pArea || !pArea2 || pArea != pArea2 )
    {
        ch_println( ch, "That range is not contained within an area." );
        return;
    }

    if ( !can_build( ch, pArea ) || !can_build( ch, pArea2 ) )
        return;

    for ( vnum = vnum1; vnum > vnum2; vnum++ )
    {
        snprintf( buf, MSL, "%d", vnum );
        do_goto( ch, buf );
    }

    return;
}

extern const MOB_DIFFICULTY_DATA mob_difficulty_levels[];
void set_mob_from_difficulty( MOB_INDEX_DATA* mob_proto )
{
    if ( mob_proto->difficulty == -1 )
    {
        // -1 means
        mob_proto->difficulty = 12;
        set_mob_from_difficulty( mob_proto );
        mob_proto->difficulty = -1;
        xSET_BIT( mob_proto->act, ACT_SAFE );
        return;
    }

    if ( mob_proto->difficulty > 0 && mob_proto->difficulty <= MAX_DIFFICULTY_LEVEL )
    {
        mob_proto->level = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].level;
        mob_proto->hitplus = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].hitplus;
        mob_proto->max_move = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].hitplus;
        mob_proto->ac = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].ac;
        mob_proto->hitroll = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].hitroll;
        mob_proto->damroll = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].damroll;
        mob_proto->numattacks = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].numattacks;
        mob_proto->perm_str = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].attr_value;
        mob_proto->perm_dex = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].attr_value;
        mob_proto->perm_con = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].attr_value;
        mob_proto->perm_int = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].attr_value;
        mob_proto->perm_wis = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].attr_value;
        mob_proto->perm_cha = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].attr_value;
        mob_proto->perm_lck = mob_difficulty_levels[mob_proto->difficulty].attr_value;
        xREMOVE_BIT( mob_proto->act, ACT_SAFE );
    }
}

CMDF do_mset( CHAR_DATA* ch, char* argument )
/* GRAL mset player frank supposedly causes bad string errors - not reproducible */
{
    char arg1 [MIL];
    char arg2 [MIL];
    char arg3 [MIL];
    char buf  [MSL];
    char outbuf[MSL];
    char cmd[MSL];
    int  num, size, plus;
    char char1, char2;
    CHAR_DATA* victim;
    ACC_CHAR* ach = NULL;
    ACCOUNT_DATA* acc = NULL;
    int value;
    RACE_DATA *race = NULL;
    int minattr, maxattr;
    bool lockvictim;
    char* origarg = argument;
    snprintf( cmd, MSL, "%s", argument );
    BUFFER_DATA* buffer = NULL;

    if ( IS_NPC( ch ) )
    {
        ch_println( ch, "Mob's can't mset" );
        return;
    }

    if ( !ch->desc )
    {
        ch_println( ch, "You have no descriptor" );
        return;
    }

    switch ( ch->substate )
    {
        default:
            break;

        case SUB_MOB_DESC:
            buffer = get_buffer( ch, FUNC );
            if ( buffer )
            {
                victim = buffer->target;
                dispose_buffer( buffer );
            }
            else
            {
                bug( "%s: NULL buffer", FUNC );
                ch->substate = SUB_NONE;
                return;
            }

            if ( !valid_char( victim ) )
            {
                ch_println( ch, "Your victim died or was extracted!" );
                stop_editing( ch, false );
                return;
            }

            SET_STRING( victim->description, copy_buffer( ch ) );

            if ( IS_NPC( victim ) && xIS_SET( victim->act, ACT_PROTOTYPE ) )
            {
                SET_STRING( victim->pIndexData->description, victim->description );
                save_mob( victim->pIndexData, true );
            }

            save_char_obj( victim, true );
            stop_editing( ch, false );
            ch->substate = ch->tempnum;
            return;

        case SUB_MOB_AIDESC:
            buffer = get_buffer( ch, FUNC );
            if ( buffer )
            {
                victim = buffer->target;
                dispose_buffer( buffer );
            }
            else
            {
                bug( "%s: NULL buffer", FUNC );
                ch->substate = SUB_NONE;
                return;
            }

            if ( !valid_char( victim ) )
            {
                ch_println( ch, "Your victim died or was extracted!" );
                stop_editing( ch, false );
                return;
            }

            SET_STRING( victim->aidescription, copy_buffer( ch ) );

            if ( IS_NPC( victim ) && xIS_SET( victim->act, ACT_PROTOTYPE ) )
            {
                SET_STRING( victim->pIndexData->aidescription, victim->aidescription );
                save_mob( victim->pIndexData, true );
            }

            save_char_obj( victim, true );
            stop_editing( ch, false );
            ch->substate = ch->tempnum;
            return;


        case SUB_MOB_LPROG:
            buffer = get_buffer( ch, FUNC );
            if ( buffer )
            {
                victim = buffer->target;
                dispose_buffer( buffer );
            }
            else
            {
                bug( "%s: NULL buffer", FUNC );
                ch->substate = SUB_NONE;
                return;
            }

            if ( !valid_char( victim ) )
            {
                ch_println( ch, "Your victim died or was extracted!" );
                stop_editing( ch, false );
                return;
            }

            MOB_INDEX_DATA* proto = victim->pIndexData;
            if ( !proto )
            {
                bug( "%s:could not find prototype!", FUNC );
                return;
            }
            SET_STRING( proto->lprog_code, copy_buffer( ch ) );
            stop_editing( ch, false );
            ch->substate = ch->tempnum;

            if ( proto->lprog_code != NULL && proto->lprog_code[0] == '\0' )
                SET_STRING( proto->lprog_code, NULL );

            save_mob( proto, true );
            save_char_obj( victim, true );
            ch_println( ch, "&WMob lua code %s.", proto->lprog_code != NULL ? "set" : "cleared" );
            LUA_PROGRAM* pLprog = get_ch_proto_lprog( proto );

            if ( pLprog )
                lua_program_dispose( pLprog );
            
            if ( !NULLSTR( proto->lprog_code ) )
            {
                LUA_PARAM params[] =
                {
                    { .type = LUA_PARAM_CHAR_PROTO, .payload = ( void* ) proto, .global_name = "self"},
                    { .type = LUA_PARAM_LAST }
                };
                // the debugger will see the output from loading the buffer, and then be unset
                // so they don't stay set. we don't have enough safety in place for that yet
                // ~Miros
                pLprog = lua_clear_debugger( lua_load_from_buffer( ch_proto_lprog_identifier( proto ), proto->lprog_code, ch, params ) );
                pLprog->mob = proto;
            }

            return;
    }

    victim = NULL;
    lockvictim = FALSE;
    smash_tilde( argument );

    if ( ch->substate == SUB_REPEATCMD )
    {
        buffer = get_buffer( ch, FUNC );
        if ( buffer )
            victim = buffer->target;
        else
        {
            bug( "%s: NULL buffer", FUNC );
            ch->substate = SUB_NONE;
            return;
        }

        if ( !valid_char( victim ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "Your victim died or was extracted!" );
            victim = NULL;
            argument = "done";
        }

        if ( argument[0] == '\0' || !str_cmp( argument, " " )
                ||   !str_cmp( argument, "stat" ) )
        {
            if ( victim )
                do_mstat( ch, victim->name );
            else
                ch_println( ch, "No victim selected.  Type '?' for help." );

            return;
        }

        if ( !str_cmp( argument, "done" ) || !str_cmp( argument, "off" ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "Mset mode off." );
            buffer = get_buffer( ch, FUNC );
            dispose_buffer( buffer );
            ch->substate = SUB_NONE;

            if ( ch->pcdata && ch->pcdata->subprompt )
                SET_STRING( ch->pcdata->subprompt, NULL );

            return;
        }
    }

    if ( victim )
    {
        lockvictim = TRUE;
        strlcpy( arg1, victim->name, MIL );
        argument = one_argument( argument, arg2 );
        strlcpy( arg3, argument, MIL );
    }
    else
    {
        lockvictim = FALSE;
        argument = one_argument( argument, arg1 );
        argument = one_argument( argument, arg2 );
        strlcpy( arg3, argument, MIL );
    }

    if ( !str_cmp( arg1, "on" ) )
    {
        ch_println( ch, "&zSyntax: &Cmset <&wvictim|vnum&C> on." );
        return;
    }

    if ( arg1[0] == '\0' || ( arg2[0] == '\0' && ch->substate != SUB_REPEATCMD ) || !str_cmp( arg1, "?" ) )
    {
        if ( ch->substate == SUB_REPEATCMD )
        {
            if ( victim )
                ch_println( ch, "&zSyntax: &C<&wfield&C> <&wvalue&C>&w" );
            else
                ch_println( ch, "&zSyntax: &C<&wvictim&C> <&wfield&C> <&wvalue&C>&w" );
        }
        else
            ch_println( ch, "&zSyntax: &Cmset <&wvictim&C> <&wfield&C> <&wvalue&C>&w" );

        ch_println( ch, "" );
        ch_println( ch, "&zField being one of:" );
        ch_println( ch, "&B  str int wis dex con cha lck frc sex" );
        ch_println( ch, "&B  credits hp force move align race skincolor droidmodel" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bhaircolor hitroll damroll armor affected level" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bthirst drunk full blood flags fclass" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bpos defpos disguise" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bsav1 sav2 sav4 sav4 sav5 &z(&wsee &CSAVINGTHROWS&z)&w" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bresistant immune susceptible &z(&wsee &CRIS&z)&w" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Battack defense numattacks lightsaberform" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bspeaking speaks tone textcolor cybers" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bname short long description title lprog spec spec2" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bspec3 spec4 clan division deposit vars owner" );
        ch_println( ch, "" );
        ch_println( ch, "&zFor editing index/prototype mobiles:" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bhitnumdie hitsizedie hitplus &z(&Chit points&z)&w" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bdamnumdie damsizedie damplus &z(&Cdamage roll&z)&w" );
        ch_println( ch, "  &Bfailed_login" );
        ch_println( ch, "" );
        ch_println( ch, "&zTo unset legacymax levels: &Cmset <player> legacymax" );
        return;
    }

    if ( !victim && get_trust( ch ) <= LEVEL_IMMORTAL )
    {
        if ( ( victim = get_char_room( ch, arg1 ) ) == NULL )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "They aren't here." );
            return;
        }
    }
    else if ( !victim )
    {
        if ( ( victim = get_char_world_full( ch, arg1 ) ) == NULL )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "No one like that in all the realms." );
            return;
        }
    }

    if ( get_trust( ch ) < get_trust( victim ) && !IS_NPC( victim ) )
    {
        ch_println( ch, "You can't mset them!" );
        return;
    }

    if ( get_trust( ch ) < sysdata.level_mset_player && !IS_NPC( victim ) && !(
        !str_cmp( arg2, "vars" ) ||
        !str_cmp( arg2, "droidmodel" ) ||
        !str_cmp( arg2, "skincolor" ) ||
        !str_cmp( arg2, "haircolor" ) ||
        !str_cmp( arg2, "sex" )
    ))
    {
        ch_println( ch, "Setting that option on players is locked to level %d and above.", sysdata.level_mset_player );
        return;
    }
    else if ( !IS_NPC( victim ) )
    {
        SET_STRING( victim->pcdata->authed_by, ch->name );
        add_mset( ch, cmd, get_trust( ch ), "Mset" );
    }

    if ( lockvictim )
    {
        buffer = get_buffer( ch, FUNC );
        if ( !buffer ) buffer = create_buffer( ch, FUNC );
        buffer->target = victim;
    }

    minattr = 1;
    maxattr = 30;

    if ( !str_cmp( arg2, "on" ) )
    {
        CHECK_SUBRESTRICTED( ch );
        ch_println( ch, "Mset mode on. (Editing %s).",
                   victim->name );
        ch->substate = SUB_REPEATCMD;
        buffer = create_buffer( ch, FUNC );
        buffer->target = victim;

        if ( ch->pcdata )
        {
            if ( IS_NPC( victim ) )
                snprintf( buf, MSL, "<&CMset &W#%d&w> %%i", victim->pIndexData->vnum );
            else
                snprintf( buf, MSL, "<&CMset &W%s&w> %%i", victim->name );

            SET_STRING( ch->pcdata->subprompt, buf );
        }

        return;
    }

    value = is_number( arg3 ) ? atoi( arg3 ) : -1;

    if ( atoi( arg3 ) < -1 && value == -1 )
        value = atoi( arg3 );

    // Gral levels now static per race; saves what you got on your roll
    //   legacymax is not manually setable use custommax
    if ( !str_cmp( arg2, "custommax" ) )
    {
        if ( !can_mmodify( ch, victim ) )
            return;

        if ( get_trust( ch ) < 105 )
            return;

        if ( IS_NPC( victim ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "Not on NPCs." );
            return;
        }

        argument = one_argument( argument, arg3 );
        int x = atoi( arg3 );

        if ( x > 11 || x < 0 || !str_cmp( arg3, "" ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "0 - Combat\n1 - Piloting\n2 - Engineering\n3 - Hunting\n4 - Smuggling\n5 - Diplomacy\n6 - Leadership\n7 - Force\n8 - Espionage\n9 - Slicer\n10 - Medic\n11 - Science" );
            return;
        }

        victim->custommax[x] = atoi( argument );
        save_char_obj( victim, true );
        ch_println( ch, "Done." );
        return;
    }

    // Gral - to unset someone's legacy max
    if ( !str_cmp( arg2, "legacymax" ) )
    {
        if ( !can_mmodify( ch, victim ) )
            return;

        if ( get_trust( ch ) < 104 )
            return;

        if ( IS_NPC( victim ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "Not on NPCs." );
            return;
        }

        int x;

        for ( x = 0; x < MAX_ABILITY; x++ )
            victim->legacymax[x] = 0;

        save_char_obj( victim, true );
        ch_println( ch, "Done." );
        return;
    }

    if ( !str_cmp( "difficulty", arg2 ) )
    {
        if ( !can_mmodify( ch, victim ) )
            return;

        if ( !IS_NPC( victim ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "NPCs only." );
            return;
        }

        if ( !xIS_SET( victim->act, ACT_PROTOTYPE ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "Difficulty can only be set on prototype mobs." );
            return;
        }

        if ( value < -1 || value > MAX_DIFFICULTY_LEVEL )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "Range is -1 to 20, with -1 being noncombat, 0 being custom, and 20 being the strongest." );
            return;
        }

        victim->pIndexData->difficulty = value;
        set_mob_from_difficulty( victim->pIndexData );
        save_mob( victim->pIndexData, true );
        ch_println( ch, "Mobile difficulty set to standard level %d."
                   "Purge and recreate the mob to refresh its stats.\n", value );
        return;
    }

    if ( !str_cmp( "fclass", arg2 ) )
    {
        if ( !can_mmodify( ch, victim ) )
            return;

        if ( IS_NPC( victim ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "Can't do that to a mob." );
            return;
        }

        if ( victim->pcdata->frank <= 0 && ( NULLSTR( arg3 ) || value != 0 ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "&zYou must set their force rank first. Use &Cmset %s frank #&z first.", victim->name );
            return;
        }

        if ( NULLSTR( arg3 ) || !is_number( arg3 ) || value < 0 || value > 8 ||
        ( value != 0 && ( ( value < 5 && victim->alignment < -300 ) || ( value > 4 && victim->alignment > 300 ) ) ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "&zSyntax: &Cmset <&wvictim&C> fclass [class #]" );
            ch_println( ch, "&zOptions: " );
            ch_println( ch, "&C0&z: None" );
            int j = victim->alignment < -300 ? 5 : 1;
            int k = victim->alignment > 300 ? 4 : 8;
            for ( int i = j; i <= k; i++ )
                ch_println( ch, "&C%d&z: %s", i, fclass(victim->pcdata->frank, i, victim->alignment ) );
            return;
        }

        victim->pcdata->fclass = value;
        ch_println( ch, "&zAlright, &C%s&z is now set to %s&z.", victim->name, victim->pcdata->fclass == 0 ? "&CNone" : fclass( victim->pcdata->frank, victim->pcdata->fclass, victim->alignment ) );
        save_char_obj( victim, true );
        FORCER_DATA* forcer = forcer_create( victim );

        if ( !forcer )
            bug( "mset %s fclass: Error saving forcer entry.", victim->name );

        return;
    }

    if ( !str_cmp( "tone", arg2 ) )
    {
        if ( !can_mmodify( ch, victim ) )
            return;

        if ( !IS_NPC( victim ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "Don't mess with a player's tone." );
            return;
        }

        DB_DATA* db = find_tone_by_name( arg3, false );

        if ( db != NULL )
        {
            victim->tone = db->id;

            if ( xIS_SET( victim->act, ACT_PROTOTYPE ) )
            {
                victim->pIndexData->tone = db->id;
                save_mob( victim->pIndexData, true );
            }

            ch_println( ch, "&zSpeaking tone for &B%s&z set to &B%s&z.", victim->name, db->name );
            save_char_obj( victim, true );
            return;
        }

        ch_println( ch, "Unrecognized tone." );
        return;
    }

    if ( !str_cmp( "cybers", arg2 ) )
    {
        if ( !can_mmodify( ch, victim ) )
            return;
        
        if ( IS_NPC( victim ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "Let's not mess with an NPC's cybernetics..." );
            return;
        }

        argument = one_argument( argument, arg3 );
        
        if ( NULLSTR( arg3 ) || ( str_cmp( arg3, "list" ) && str_cmp( arg3, "remove" ) ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "&zSyntax: &Cmset %s cybers list", victim->name );
            ch_println( ch, "&z        &Cmset %s cybers remove <&wcyber&C>", victim->name );
            return;
        }

        if ( !victim->first_cyber )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "&C%s&z doesn't have any cybernetics installed.", victim->name );
            return;
        }

        CYBER_DATA* chcyber = NULL;
        int cycnt = 0;

        if ( !str_cmp( "list", arg3 ) )
        {
            ch_println( ch, "&zListing cybernetics for &C%s&z...", victim->name );
            for ( chcyber = victim->first_cyber; chcyber; chcyber = chcyber->next_on_char )
            {
                ch_println( ch, "\n&C%d: &W%s", ++cycnt, chcyber->cyber_index->longdesc );
                for ( AFFECT_DATA* aff = chcyber->cyber_index->first_affect; aff; aff = aff->next )
                    showaffect( ch, aff );
            }

            ch_println( ch, "\n&zDisplayed &C%d&z cybernetics.", cycnt );
            return;
        }

        if ( !str_cmp( "remove", arg3 ) )
        {
            for ( chcyber = victim->first_cyber; chcyber; chcyber = chcyber->next_on_char )
                if ( stristr( chcyber->cyber_index->longdesc, argument ) || ( is_number( argument ) && atoi( argument ) == ++cycnt ) )
                    break;
            
            if ( !chcyber )
            {
                ch_println( ch, "%s doesn't have that cybernetic installed.", victim->name );
                return;
            }
            char cyber_arg[MIL];
            strlcpy( cyber_arg, chcyber->cyber_index->longdesc, MIL );
            bool result = uninstall_cyber( victim, chcyber->cyber_index->name );
            int iClass = 0, tmplevel = 0;
            for ( iClass = 0; iClass < MAX_ABILITY; iClass++ )
            {
                tmplevel = victim->skill_level[iClass];
                victim->skill_level[iClass] = URANGE( 1, victim->skill_level[iClass], max_level_flag( victim, iClass, TRUE ) );
                if ( tmplevel > victim->skill_level[iClass] )
                    victim->experience[iClass] = exp_level( victim->skill_level[iClass] + 1 ) - 1;                
            }

            LEARNED_DATA* learned = NULL, *next_learned = NULL;
            SKILL_DATA* skill = NULL;
            for ( learned = victim->first_learned; learned; learned = next_learned )
            {
                next_learned = learned->next;
                skill = learned->skill;
